The agent applies a request once per mutation identity and only for the version it names, and refuses it while a run is unfinished; a change from elsewhere moves the version on. Whether an applied removal moves the version is not assumed, so a repeat is answered from the receipt alone.

At most two copies of one request are in flight; a third send stands for the loss of one. Requests of an earlier change still in flight when a new one is sent are dropped: they name an older version or already have a receipt.
The resend reads the receipt before posting and again after a refusal; both reads are folded into the resend and refusal steps.
Pending trigger cleanup, which blocks a restore, and agents without reviewed removal are not modeled.
An account change resets the view; the retained request belongs to its account and is not modeled across accounts.
The run history on screen is at most one run. A run that starts after the workflow was opened is unknown to the phone until the next read; the agent's refusal is what stops a change sent meanwhile.

stateMapping.account/client: connectionController.getCloudClient sessionId and credentialId (the account) and the client object bound to it
stateMapping.generation/inflight/configured/error/ins: createCloudMaps generation, attempts in flight, diagnostic.configured, diagnostic.error and installed
stateMapping.ownerAccount/ownerClient: captureMapsSession owner session and credential over mapsSession, and the client object bound when the provider was installed (bookkeeping: the provider holds accountClient, not that object)
stateMapping.opened/guidance/guidanceEnd/lastRequest: MapsScreenController initialized, navigating, the cause of its release and the outcome of one provider request
stateMapping.servedClient: the client accountClient.mapsRequest and the tileRequest closure resolve from getCloudClient for one request

abstractions: Two accounts, six read generations and five client objects; account changes, reconnects and reads are disabled at the bounds rather than dropped.
Failure codes are two classes: unauthorized (signed out or a changed binding) and transient (every other refused read). No timer retries a failed read; an explicit search or map retry does.

The account-change retirement in cloud-maps.ts and the coverage reader's microtask are one step, in that order. The resident stays ready once it is ready. The regional test gateway, the assistant window and map tiles are not modeled.
Guidance is one flag owned by the Maps screen: retiring the installed provider releases the screen and ends it.
unguardedRead is outside step. It replays a read issued over a working provider, which ends guidance; readKeepsGuidanceTest shows the guarded read keeping it.

pinnedClientRequest is outside step. It replays a provider that keeps the client object its coverage was read with, whose requests are refused after the same account is bound with a rebuilt client; rebuiltClientKeepsRequestsWorkingTest shows it breaking RebuiltClientKeepsProviderWorking and the per-request client serving the same request.

Search, route and tile requests are one request action: all three compare session and credential only and use the client bound at the time of the call. A reply landing after an account change is covered by retirement, not by a separate late-reply step.

stateMapping.searching/hasQuery/selected/directions/o: MapsScreenController flags behind MapsScreenView.mode, mapped to the template's base, results, place, dir, origin and nav; selected distinguishes a provider place, a saved place and the located position
stateMapping.results: MapsController search phase ready: the rows a result pick needs
stateMapping.locating/watch: MapsScreenController.locating and the controller's one-fix NativeMapsLocation watch
stateMapping.originText/origin/routeReady: MapsScreenController.originText (empty, a typed name, coordinates, a chosen candidate's name or "Your location"), MapsController origin and a ready route
stateMapping.screenOff/hidden: BackgroundNavigation.active() without and with the screen's confirmed session, and document visibility as seen by screen.hidden
stateMapping.lastChoice: history only: the destination's most recent explicit choice, for the property outside safety
stateMapping.handoffQuery/handoffPending/requests/han: the Maps view's one-use query, the adapter's pendingHandoff and the searches screen.handoff ran

abstractions: One provider place, one saved place and one origin candidate. Place detail, travel modes, route choices, renaming, sharing, recentering, the map plane and the installed maps app hand-off are not modeled.

openDirections is the route sheet opened without the location permission, or with a starting point typed before the permission read settles; openGrantedDirections is the granted read, which asks for one fix when the starting point is empty and no route exists.

leave is another launcher view taking the screen with Maps coming straight back: settled places, the route sheet and guidance are kept, a pending location request and any request in flight are not. Guidance away from Maps is in MapsNavigationGuidanceReadback.

A hidden page keeps guidance only while its screen-off session is reserved or running; otherwise guidance ends and the route sheet stays. A full release happens for a cross-app search and when the session ends or is refused on a hidden page. A location-permission prompt that keeps a hidden Maps screen is in NavigationProgress and NativeMapsLocation.

Enter on the located position's text, the fifteen-second location time limit, reroutes and arrival are not modeled. The route request is one outcome action; leaving and hiding abort it and the replay plans again before settling one.
The hand-off microtask is an action that can be delayed. Every newer explicit action discards the pending hand-off, so a delayed one finds nothing to run.

LateFixKeepsNewerChoiceDesired is outside safety: typing a search or picking a saved place does not end a pending location request, so its fix replaces that choice. lateFixReplacesUnsubmittedChoiceTest replays it.

stateMapping.pickers/started/ended: The systemPickers counter around each picker or export call
stateMapping.hidden/hiddenUnderPicker: document.hidden and whether a picker was in flight when the page became hidden
stateMapping.review/document/searchable/correction/ca: The five scan dialogs; the first three are exempt from the hidden-page close while a picker is open
stateMapping.generation/live/pending/retired/delivere: The owned browser file picker controller, operating-system results still outstanding, and results delivered to a consumer

abstractions: Three picker calls and three browser file pickers. pagehide closes every dialog and cancels the owned file picker.
A picker that settles while the page stays hidden produces no further hidden event; the dialog then stays until the page is shown or unloaded.

Trace replay: test/quint-system-picker-visibility.test.mjs replays simulator traces step by step against duringSystemPicker, systemPickerActive and runFilePicker; the five scan dialogs are not mounted, so the hidden-page close rules are checked by the model only and compares the observed state after every step. It is bounded evidence for the sampled traces, not a refinement proof or device acceptance.

stateMapping.text: OCR state, the one-shot Notes save latch, photo PDF attempt and lock, Keep photo state and retries, and the nested document dialog
stateMapping.searchable: ready, busy and requested flags and the result the review resolves with
stateMapping.correction: busy work, corner edits, the preview and the corners it was made from
stateMapping.capture: Camera stream state, frame encoding, the reviewed capture and the returned page

abstractions: The four dialogs are independent machines in one module; their hidden-page rules are in SystemPickerVisibility and document drafts are in ScanDocument.
Corner positions are an edit counter. Keep photo outcomes are saved, retryable and unconfirmed as the host reports them.
Retake needs a live camera, so a capture reviewed before the camera stopped is kept.
Model safety checks do not establish implementation refinement or device acceptance.

stateMapping.viewOpen/hidden/picking/active/lifecycle: installSmsAdapter sync(): Messages in front, or hidden only while the picture chooser it opened is up; the visit token
stateMapping.chooser/chooserLifecycle/chooserDraft: the file input attach() opened, with the visit and draft revision it captured; done() ends the pick on a visible page or on pagehide
stateMapping.pictures/draftRevision/edits: attachments (at most MMS_MAX_ATTACHMENTS) and the draft revision every edit, removal, pick and closed answer advances
stateMapping.operationId/minted: mmsOperationId, minted by crypto.randomUUID() only when the draft holds none; resetMms clears it
stateMapping.call/callLifecycle/callDraft/reply: client.sendMms in flight with the token and draft it captured, and the native answer not yet received
stateMapping.journal/dispatches: the native MMS send record per operation ID and the single platform dispatch behind it (NativeMmsDispatch)
stateMapping.shown/shownFrom/shownLifecycle: the notice from the draft, a send answer or reconcileMms()
stateMapping.operationId/lastSent/draftReady: Actual closure-observed current draft identity/readiness, separate from the last accepted receipt identity. Accepted sends retire the current draft; uncertain unfinished drafts retain their exact ID privately across visits.

abstractions: Three operation IDs, six visits, bounded draft revisions and picks of one or three pictures. Recipients, text and SIM are one draft; review refusals before the native call (no SIM, too large, MMS unavailable) are not modeled.

Owner controls and each native send require the current visible page. One chooser is open at a time; an already admitted call may await settlement behind it. The SMS operation ID, which the same edits reset, is SmsSend.
The journal is one status per ID; the reviewed binding, PDU custody and carrier evidence are NativeMmsDispatch. The foreground provider session is the shared telephony session.
Replayed against installSmsAdapter with a held telephony client and a held file input (test/quint-mms-compose.test.mjs); no SIM, carrier, chooser activity or installed-image claim.

AP-05 retains unfinished owner drafts in memory across lifecycle changes. Inactive visits have no current review/send/publication authority. Readback may name the held ID or last accepted receipt; it cannot grant a new draft authority. Native request ports assert current foreground admission, and explicit empty/retired-send canaries require zero new native requests or carrier effects.

stateMapping.exists/enabled/runs: one prompt automation on the agent and the runs it started
stateMapping.loaded/complete/knownExists/knownEnabled: the list read for the current connection, whether every source answered, and the row as read
stateMapping.retained/busy/unknown: the journal entry of the change, the operation sending it, and the unknown-outcome lock on the row
stateMapping.flight/reply: requests on the network, including one that outlived its journal entry, and the answer to the newest
stateMapping.lastRelease/releasedKind/releasedOn/late: why the latest entry was released, of what kind, on what list, and whether a released enable request later changed the row

abstractions: One prompt automation and three changes. Reminder edits settle by the same rule (every requested field matches a complete reminders source) and are not distinguished.
A definite refusal stands for the status codes the adapter treats as a known non-change and for a block raised before dispatch.
New items, snooze and fire share the run request: a list never settles them.
The scheduled-task verbs of the same list are modeled in ScheduledTaskControls.
A list that shows the requested enabled value releases the entry although its request may still be in flight; LateEnableOverridesWitness records that such a request can later undo a newer choice.

stateMapping.enabled/held/spoken/speaking: the shared speaker's enabled, current, spoken and the speech its owner controller has in flight
stateMapping.hidden/speechHidden: document.hidden and the hiddenDuringSpeech flag of one speech call
stateMapping.epoch/sheetOpen: the session, resident inference, provider revision, Cloud environment, Cloud session and credential and connection mode an instruction captured, and the snapshot's open
stateMapping.latest/minted: NavigationVoice.latest and the instruction objects created
stateMapping.owed/listening: NavigationVoice.owed and the resume handler registered for visibilitychange
stateMapping.starts/failures: speech requests that reached app speech or the on-device voice, and failed() calls

abstractions: Three guidance steps, six instruction objects and three context changes. A step's key and text change together.
Speech outcomes are three classes: finished, a provider failure, and an abort the caller did not ask for. An abort through the speech's own signal is ignored by the speaker and is not an event.
An unconfirmed speech cleanup counts as a provider failure. Cloud and on-device speech are one port.
The microtask that resumes an instruction owed on a visible page is part of the step that owed it.
A newer instruction issued on a hidden page under a changed context does not replace the owed one; the return to the front then speaks neither.
Changes that end guidance or its context are drawn one time in four so sampled traces reach resumed speech.

stateMapping.navigation/registrations: residentMapsNavigationPort.current and the bindings registered on it
stateMapping.turns: one withResidentMapsNavigation call: its opening request, whether its offer is open while the message is sent, its poll in flight, and the binding it began with

abstractions: Three turns and three navigation bindings. A turn without a resident request or without a registered binding sends its message with nothing offered.
A refused offer and a failed opening request are one outcome; both retire the offer before the message is sent.
Navigation requests served during a turn (select, start, reroute, stop) and their results are in MapsNavigation; here a connected turn only receives or not.
Turn cancellation and the best-effort retirement request are not modeled.
unlatchedEnd is outside step: an end that clears the flag whichever turn owns it.
ConnectedTurnShowsFlagDesired is outside safety: when two turns overlap and the one accepted last ends first, the other stays connected with the flag cleared. The flag is diagnostic output only.

stateMapping.state.*: Actual pending approval, timer, task store, settled result and each invocation program counter; refused callback/stop errors and dispatched deletion identities are observed independently.
stateMapping.pendingWork/stopDone: Actual RuntimeRetirement pending operation count and stop promise settlement, including the original approval request and nested worker/selection operations.

abstractions: Selected current-source synchronous callback-bearing approvals, two selector identities, one task and one controlled deadline. Source replay retains every historical PC/effect observation and adds refusal and draining-stop observations.

Task creation races, role checks, asynchronous callback-free persisted approvals, failed storage writes and arbitrary approval counts remain outside this bounded component; this is not complete implementation refinement.
Temporal properties assume weak fairness of admitted callback and storage continuations; unresponsive ports can intentionally keep stop pending.

stateMapping.version/name: the agent's workflow: its version and the change that last named it
stateMapping.knownVersion/knownName/opened: the workflow detail this phone last read, and whether the workflow is open
stateMapping.editor/editorVersion: the name and description editor and the version it was opened on
stateMapping.intent/intentVersion: the retained metadata request (metadataKey) with the version it names; the journal keeps the identity of the change, not its text
stateMapping.busy/stage/reply: the workflow operation in progress, whether the request has been sent, and the answer waiting for it
stateMapping.wire/wireId/wireVersion: the newest request on the network, with the change and version it names
stateMapping.receipts: the changes the agent applied and keeps a receipt for, by mutation identity
stateMapping.seen/checked/sent/admissions/application: whether this phone learned of the applied change, whether its receipt was read since the app started, sends of the newest change, and totals

abstractions: One workflow and three edits. Name and description change together; the name stands for both.
The agent applies a change once per mutation identity and only for the version it names, and each applied change moves the version on. A change from elsewhere also moves it.
One copy of a change is in flight at most: nothing resends a metadata change. A request of an earlier change still in flight names an older version or has its receipt and is dropped.
Leaving the editor before the journal write refuses the write; the model records and releases the entry in one step with the same end state.

Agents without metadata editing, length limits on the fields, and workflows edited through typed authoring (WorkflowAuthoring) are not modeled. A retained change belongs to its account and is not modeled across accounts.
